text: This is our final step, before we are actually able to transmit and receive data, to and from the access point. What is this association? Now remember, the user is authenticated with an access point. So what, access point and user, the user is also called, remember, WiFi station. What we do is to get to know each other, okay? So the meaning of this step is to exchange some basic information about themselves. So the user will say, well, I have this WiFi card, of course, we'd say, I can implement this version of the standard. And the access point will do the same, we'd say, I can implement this version of the standard. The user will also say, I'd like to transmit this kind of data, okay? That that may require certain quality of of service. Or what they also say is, the user can tell the access point, if it's part, if that access point is part of an extended service set. The user can tell the access point, look, I was previously connected to this other access point within the same ESS. So if you are on campus and you walk, as you walk, you may move from one access point to another. You don't realize that.
